    Group

    Postdoctoral research assistants and fellows

    • Dr Stephanie Abo - Data-driven modelling of collective cell behaviour.
    • Dr Torkel Loman - Practical identifiability of mathematical models.

    Doctoral students

    • Jamie Boyle – Data-driven modelling of collective cell migration. (Joint with Helen Byrne.)
    • Arianna Ceccarelli – Mathematical approaches to mRNA transport and localisation. (Joint with Alex Browning.)
    • Katie Croft – Computational modelling of hematopoietic stem cell maintenance during physiological ageing and inflammatory stress. (Joint with Claus Nerlov.)
    • Rebecca Crossley – Continuum models of cell invasion. (Joint with Philip Maini.)
    • Carles Falco I Gandia – Modelling interacting cell populations (Joint with Jose Carrillo.)
    • James Hammond –  On the evolvability of segment number in Teleost fishes. (Joint with Berta Verd.)
    • Elliot Hughes – Mathematical modelling of cell migration. (Joint with Sarah Waters.)
    • Samuel Johnson  – Mathematical modelling of neural crest cell invasion. (Joint with  Philip Maini.)
    • Ian McFarlane  –  Homeostasis, bacterial infection and carcinogenesis in human gastric glands. (Joint with Helen Byrne and  Francesco Boccellato.)
    • Joseph Pollaco  –  A hybrid experimental-modelling study of SOS response-induced filamentation and its effect on bacterial colony growth . (Joint with Stefan Uphoff and  Philip Maini.)
    • Tom Quinlan – An integrative mathematical approach to understand how intraplaque angiogenesis and vascular structure impact atherosclerosis and their potential as novel therapeutic targets. (Joint with Helen Byrne.)
    • Thomas Reed – Mathematical modelling of adipose tissue lipid metabolism. (Joint with Helen Byrne.)
    • Nathan Schofield – Mathematical modelling of the role of cell heterogeneity in promoting melanoma metastasis. (Joint with Helen Byrne and Richard White.)
    • Yuan Yin – Mathematical modelling of cardiac fibrosis. (Joint with Sarah Waters.)
